artifacts.summary: All 8 plan phases closed: dispatch-strand-probe.sh plus its three consumers (postflight's stranded_suspected, the lead's re-prompt relay, reconcile's demotion gate), per-context held-live documentation, and the await-a-notification prevention lint (Check K).

completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented dispatch-strand-probe.sh (a read-only heartbeat+quiescence conjunction probe) and wired it into orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's new stranded_suspected field, skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md's existing one-re-prompt relay, and reconcile-task-status.sh's demotion gate -- so a stranded dispatch is detected and recovered before any failure is charged. Extended lint-agent-contracts.sh with Check K to mechanically reject the detach-then-await-a-notification antipattern. Found and fixed two regressions during Phase 8's full-gate verification (a test's section-scoping boundary, and a SKILL.md eager-load ceiling overrun) before redeploying.

memory_candidates.content: task-lock.sh check's held-live state (stale heartbeat, live holder pid) has OPPOSITE correct interpretations depending on consumer context: during lock acquisition a live pid means 'do not steal, a session may be working'; during dispatch monitoring the SAME observation is the strand signature, because the heartbeat staleness (not the pid) is doing the discriminating work, and a live pid is weak evidence there (ancestor claude pids are shared across sessions). When building a monitoring-context consumer of an acquisition-context signal, never assume the acquisition-context reading transfers -- check which question the context is actually asking.

A grep/sed-based test that scopes its assertions to one check's output section by bounding on a generic end-marker (e.g. the final '======== Summary' divider) silently swallows every later check's output into that section once a new check is inserted after it in the lint's main(). Bound section-extraction on 'the next sibling header OR the final divider', not the divider alone, whenever a lint script's checks run in a fixed, extensible order.

Editing a skill/agent markdown file that carries a per-file eager-load byte ceiling (orchestrator-context-budget.json) can silently push it over, and that FAIL only surfaces at redeploy/verify-deploy time, not at edit time -- there is no earlier signal. After any non-trivial prose addition to a budget-tracked file (e.g. skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md), check `wc -c` against the configured ceiling_bytes before considering the edit done, rather than discovering the regression only during the final gate run.
